claims.text: A hierarchical microstructure containing a lubricious phase dispersed within a harder matrix can be created in CoCrFeNi.
The hierarchical microstructure will maintain a low coefficient of friction from room temperature to 800 °C.
The hierarchical microstructure will maintain a low wear rate from room temperature to 800 °C.
Low friction and wear will be maintained under varying loads and environments.
The lubricious phase will form pathways for easy sliding.
The lubricious pathways will reduce friction.
The harder matrix will provide mechanical support.
The harder matrix will provide wear resistance.
The modified CoCrFeNi material will have a lower coefficient of friction than the starting CoCrFeNi material.
The modified CoCrFeNi material will have a lower wear rate than the starting CoCrFeNi material.
The lubricious phase will be most effective at high temperatures.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis claims maintained performance throughout room temperature to 800 °C, but the falsification rule considers only temperatures above 500 °C; failure at room temperature through 500 °C would therefore not falsify the stated full-range claim.
